answer: An AI-agent economy can curb Sybil attacks via fiber-optic link attestation. A verifier sends an optical probe signal down each node's strand, requiring it to modulate a signed nonce onto the return wave while matching the fiber's Rayleigh interference ripple and thermal phase wander. Since clones sharing one strand yield identical profiles, attackers incur dedicated fiber, transceiver, and power costs per identity. However, cable splices shift the baseline and reject valid nodes.
